title: The Substantial sum for the work
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：substantial　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 substantial 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the craftsman wrote of ① a substantial sum for the work in the ledger, and everybody in the workshop said at once that it was ② so substantial that nobody in the workshop would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the craftsman, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the substantial ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the substantial sum for the work that anybody there had ever seen, or so the ledger for August 1970 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too substantial to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the apprentice who had come to help; the substantial ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a substantial change in the rules, and said that no apprentice in his right mind would call it ⑥ as substantial as the change in the rules they had once had in the old workshop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was substantial or not, and he said so.

By 1983 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the ledger. What the line asked for was ⑦ something substantial, and nothing besides. The apprentice from the next workshop called the whole plan ⑧ quite substantial; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the ledger kept the names of the substantial ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1986, in public, she wrote of another substantial sum for the work in the same ledger, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less substantial than anybody had expected. ⑩ The substantial change in the rules that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1988, was the one she could never quite name; the substantial ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 大量（前置定语 a substantial sum for the work：1976 年匠人在工料簿里记下的那件大量的报酬）
B. adj. 大量／实质性（两处加强说法：so substantial that … 与 no less substantial than …）
C. adj. 大量／实质性（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 大量（表语 too substantial to do：母亲觉得它太大量，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 实质性（前置定语 a substantial change in the rules：叔叔把整件事称作一桩实质性的实质改动）
F. adj. 实质性（同级比较 as substantial as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩规矩上的实质改动相比）
G. adj. 实质性（后置定语 something substantial：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 实质性（受程度副词修饰 quite substantial：那位学徒的评价）

items.q: a substantial sum for the work
the substantial sum for the work that
a substantial change in the rules
The substantial change in the rules that

answers.why: substantial 意为“大量”，1976 年匠人在工料簿里记下的是“一件大量的报酬”，此处作前置定语 a substantial sum for the work。
substantial 意为“大量”，此处用 so substantial that 结构，说它大量到工坊里没人敢靠近。
substantial 意为“大量”，工料簿上 八月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的大量一笔可观的报酬，等于最高级的说法。
substantial 意为“大量”，母亲认为这件东西“太大量了，谁也用不上”，too substantial to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
substantial 意为“实质性”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩实质性的实质改动”，此处作前置定语 a substantial change in the rules。
substantial 意为“实质性”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩规矩上的实质改动一样实质性”，同级比较用 as substantial as。
substantial 意为“实质性”，工料簿上那半行字要的是“实质性的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something substantial。
substantial 意为“实质性”，邻工坊来的那位学徒认为这套计划“相当实质性”，quite 修饰原级 substantial。
substantial 意为“实质性”，no less substantial than 表示“其实质性不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之实质性不亚于任何人的预料。
substantial 意为“实质性”，母亲 1988 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的实质性实质改动”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1976 年，匠人在工料簿里记下了一件大量的报酬。（a substantial sum for the work）
它大量到工坊里没有一个人敢靠近。（so substantial that …）
母亲觉得它太大量，谁也用不上。（too substantial to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩实质性的实质改动。（a substantial change in the rules）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩规矩上的实质改动一样实质性。（as substantial as …）
到了 1983 年，工料簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件实质性的东西。（something substantial）
answers: In 1976 the craftsman wrote of a substantial sum for the work in the ledger.
It was so substantial that nobody in the workshop would go near it.
My mother thought it too substantial to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a substantial change in the rules.
He said nobody would call it as substantial as the change in the rules they had once had.
By 1983 the ledger asked for nothing but something substantial.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 substantial 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the craftsman wrote of a substantial sum for the work in the ledger, and nobody forgot it.
It was the substantial sum for the work that anybody there had ever seen, or so the ledger says.
My mother thought it too substantial to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a substantial change in the rules, and nobody argued with him.
The apprentice from the next workshop called the plan quite substantial, and everybody laughed.
The substantial ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
